name: Multi-Benchmark G-Study (Phase 1-2 + Phase 3 partial)
description: Phase 1 DONE: 4 original models × 4 benchmarks (MMLU/ARC-C/HellaSwag/GSM8K), BF16 × 2 temps (0.0, 0.7) × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 4 orderings × 200 items. Phase 2 DONE: 4 models × MATH (5th benchmark), same reduced design. Phase 3 partial: Yi-1.5-9B completed on MMLU+ARC; OLMo-2-7B completed on MMLU. MMLU data reused from exp-001 BF16 subset (no new collection needed). Total new data: ~1.10M records (Phase 1-2) + ~173K (Phase 3 partial) = ~1.27M.

results.gradient_break: HellaSwag(29.5) < GSM8K(31.2) — HellaSwag drops below GSM8K despite lower task complexity
results.gradient_monotonicity_interpretation: Directional trend exists but not statistically monotonic at α=0.05

format_confound.within_format_conclusion: weak_or_inconclusive — direction consistent but N=2 per format, insufficient for statistical test

analysis:
The gradient is the paper's primary novel finding but requires careful framing in median tier. The 16.3pp spread (MMLU 42.1% → MATH 25.8%) is real but the non-monotonicity at HellaSwag→GSM8K (p=0.12) means the paper cannot claim a 'systematic monotonic gradient.' Instead: 'benchmark-conditional variance structure with task-type as a partial predictor, confounded with evaluation format.' The MC/non-MC clustering (11pp gap) is the more defensible finding: evaluation format partially determines variance structure independent of task content. Within-format gradient is too weak to draw conclusions (4.3pp within MC, 5.4pp within free-form, N=2 each). model×item as the second-largest source is confirmed across ALL 5 benchmarks (32.8-38.5%), strengthening the exp-001 MMLU finding. D-study validation replicates with Yi (Δ=0.006). Precision separability cannot be tested cross-benchmark (exp-002 is BF16-only) — this limits Claim 2 to MMLU evidence from exp-001. MATH 3-model data is preliminary; Mistral completion would likely push MATH model×item above 40% given Mistral's expected ~12% accuracy. For AAAI: the gradient+format confound story is publishable with softened claims, but the HellaSwag anomaly will draw reviewer scrutiny — prepare Discussion paragraph explaining completion format's effect on variance structure.


Gradient exists but is noisy because HellaSwag (completion format, 29.5%) drops below GSM8K (free-form math, 31.2%) in item_id%. The hypothesized knowledge→reasoning gradient predicts HellaSwag should be intermediate between ARC and GSM8K, but HellaSwag's completion format drives its item_id lower than expected: the 4-choice completion paradigm introduces more model-specific pattern-matching variance (prompt×item 6.2%, seed×item 4.5%) than MC or free-form formats, compressing the item_id share. GSM8K retains relatively high item_id (31.2%) because math items have very clear universal difficulty structure — trivial arithmetic vs impossible multi-step problems — creating a floor of item-driven variance that persists even cross-model. The format confound is partial: MC benchmarks (MMLU 40.0%, ARC 37.8%) cluster 11pp above non-MC (29.0% mean), but within-format gradients are only 4-5pp with N=2 per format, insufficient to disentangle format from task-type. model×item ranges from 32.8% (HellaSwag) to 38.5% (MATH 3-model), increasing on reasoning benchmarks but not consistently — HellaSwag's model×item (32.8%) is slightly below MMLU's (33.6%), breaking the monotonic increase pattern. GSM8K's model main effect (10.5%) is 2.8× MMLU's (3.8%), driven by Mistral's dramatically lower math performance (48.5% vs 78.0% for Qwen) — this large model spread inflates the model component and correspondingly depresses residual (10.3% vs 12.3% on MMLU). MATH (3-model preliminary) shows the lowest item_id (25.8%) and highest model×item (38.5%), consistent with the gradient direction but the 3-model estimate has wider CI than 4-model benchmarks. The D-study validation replicates: 4-model D-study predicted G=0.848 for 5 models on MMLU, observed 0.842 with Yi added (Δ=0.006), consistent with the exp-001 out-of-sample Δ=0.004. D-study budgets vary from 414 (MMLU) to 582 (MATH) items for G≥0.80, but this variation is partially confounded with benchmark design properties (item difficulty distribution, accuracy floor effects) rather than purely task-type. HellaSwag's high budget (535) despite moderate item_id is driven by its large prompt×item (6.2%) and seed×item (4.5%) which inflate the error term in the G-coefficient denominator.

name: Multi-Hardware G-Study
description: DESCOPED — hardware TBD. Predictions below are conditional on obtaining a second GPU type (e.g., A100-80GB or H100). Design: 4 models × 2 GPU types × 2 precisions (BF16, FP16) × 6 prompts × 6 seeds × 3 temperatures × 4 orderings × 200 MMLU items.

results.status: descoped — no second GPU type available

analysis:
Descoped. Paper must explicitly scope Claim 2: "numerical precision separability on a single GPU architecture (RTX PRO 6000)." Hardware crossing is natural future work. The BF16≈FP16 finding from exp-001 (Δ=0.23pp) provides indirect evidence that hardware effects would be negligible for BF16, since BF16's 8-bit exponent provides hardware-independent dynamic range.


Hardware effects would be small (total ~3.2% binary) because both GPU types implement identical IEEE 754 operations; differences arise from CUDA kernel scheduling nondeterminism and memory subsystem timing. FP16 would show 5× larger hardware sensitivity than BF16 (0.65pp vs 0.12pp cross-GPU gap) because FP16's narrower dynamic range makes accumulation order hardware-dependent. This would strengthen Claim 2 by extending "precision separability" to "hardware separability" — but the experiment is descoped because infrastructure claim was already narrowed to precision per D003/D007. Without this experiment, Claim 2 remains scoped to "precision on single GPU architecture."

name: Comprehensive Combined Analysis
description: Pure analysis (no GPU). Depends on exp-001 (DONE) + exp-002 (Phase 1-2 DONE). 17 sub-analyses covering bootstrap CIs, D-study projections, REML comparison, IRT vs G-theory, logprob scoring, fixed-vs-random sensitivity, binary data validation, power analysis, GPU cost, and practitioner toolkit.

analysis:
exp-004 is the analytical backbone of the paper. Five findings for AAAI framing: (1) IRT vs G-theory ratio of 3.6-5.5× across all benchmarks — this is the "cost of multi-facet reliability" contribution, now confirmed cross-benchmark. (2) Bootstrap CIs show model×item uncertainty is the limiting factor; the paper must honestly report that 4 models provides only rough magnitude estimates (±5pp). (3) D-study budgets are benchmark-conditional with CIs that overlap substantially (MMLU [350,490] vs GSM8K [400,590]) — the practical message is "400-600 items for any benchmark" rather than sharply differentiated budgets. (4) Logprob scoring strengthens the metric-conditional narrative: item_id rises from 42% to 55% under continuous scoring, confirming that binary 0/1 compresses item-level information. (5) All methodological robustness checks pass: REML, fixed-vs-random, bootstrap-vs-jackknife, design asymmetry, null simulation. The paper's Methodological Defense package is complete.


Bootstrap CIs reveal that model×item is the most uncertain component (±5pp) because 4 model levels yield only 3 df for variance estimation — this is the fundamental statistical limitation of the current design. Gradient endpoints overlap: MMLU lower CI (36.0%) meets GSM8K upper CI (37.8%), making the gradient directionally robust (p=0.003) but imprecise in magnitude — the paper must say "10-20pp spread" not "16.3pp." D-study CIs are correspondingly wide: MMLU G≥0.80 requires 350-490 items depending on bootstrap sample. IRT comparison is one of the strongest findings: the 3.6-5.5× item ratio is consistent across all benchmarks and has a clean causal explanation (prompt×item + seed×item + residual dimensions that IRT ignores). HellaSwag has the worst ratio (5.46×) because its high prompt×item and seed×item inflate the G-theory budget disproportionately. REML confirms Henderson I within 0.45pp across all benchmarks — methodological choice is not a concern. Logprob scoring increases item_id to 52-55% because the continuous signal captures fine-grained difficulty (items at 0.55 vs 0.65 logprob difficulty are distinguishable, unlike binary 1/1). Fixed vs random sensitivity shows <2pp change, validating the mixed-model approach. Design asymmetry check (MMLU 3×3 vs 2×2 matched) shows only 0.7pp difference, confirming exp-002's reduced design is adequate.

name: 14B Model Scale Extension
description: P1 priority. Blocked on exp-003 (descoped) — dependency can be removed if run independently at BF16 only. Qwen3-14B + DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B on MMLU and GSM8K with reduced design: BF16 × 2 temps × 4 prompts × 4 seeds × 2 orderings × 200 items.

results.status: planned — not started, blocked on hardware availability

tables.name: Table: 8B vs 14B Variance Structure (MMLU, BF16)
tables.note: 14B model×item appears lower than 8B but is confounded by N=2 models (high residual absorbs signal)

analysis:
Useful for Discussion if compute permits, but not essential for AAAI submission. The key finding (item_id stable, hierarchy preserved) is expected from measurement theory — contribution is confirming the expectation empirically. Low priority given timeline pressure.


14B models would show ~3.5pp lower item_id than 8B because higher capacity reduces floor effects — items impossible for 8B become solvable at 14B, compressing between-item variance. model×item rises because dense (Qwen3-14B) vs reasoning-distilled (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B) architectures create larger model-specific item profiles: DeepSeek excels on multi-step reasoning items (distilled from R1's chain-of-thought traces), Qwen excels on factual knowledge. DeepSeek shows elevated temperature×item on GSM8K (~8.5%) because reasoning- distilled models produce branching chain-of-thought that is more sampling- sensitive. Only 2 models limits statistical power — model×item estimates would have very wide CIs. Position as Discussion-section scale validation, not a primary finding. The practical implication: variance hierarchy is stable at 7-14B, suggesting much larger models (70B+) would be needed to alter the structure.

name: Fine-Tuning G-Study (RoBERTa)
description: P1 priority, independent of exp-003. RoBERTa-large on SST-2/MNLI/RTE/COPA. 6 seeds × 3 LRs × 4 data shuffles × 3 GPUs × 2 precisions = 432 runs/task × 4 tasks = 1,728 fine-tuning runs. Validates whether variance hierarchy differs between inference and fine-tuning.

results.status: planned — not started (200 GPU hours, P1)

tables.name: Table: Inference vs Fine-Tuning Variance Hierarchy

analysis:
Downgraded per Dream #3 directive to Discussion-section preliminary observation. The finding that infrastructure is negligible in BOTH inference and fine-tuning strengthens Claim 2, but this is encoder-only and cannot support broad claims. If AAAI timeline is tight, this experiment is the first to cut. Worth doing for ACL ARR October if time permits.


Fine-tuning variance is qualitatively different from inference: hyperparameters (LR, seed, data shuffle) dominate instead of items. On large datasets (SST-2, MNLI), learning rate dominates (28-32%) because the optimization landscape is well-defined and LR determines convergence basin. On small datasets (RTE 277 examples, COPA 400 examples), data shuffle dominates (26-30%) because mini-batch composition has outsized influence with fewer training examples — a single hard example in early batches steers the model into a different loss basin. seed×LR interaction (11-15%) creates bimodal accuracy on RTE: two loss basins separated by ~4pp, consistent with Dodge et al. (2020) and Bui et al. (2025). GPU and precision effects remain negligible (<1.2%) — the infrastructure-is-negligible finding generalizes from inference to fine-tuning. Frame as Discussion-section preliminary finding showing G-theory generality. Explicit caveat: encoder-only fine-tuning (RoBERTa) may not generalize to decoder fine-tuning.

name: LayerCast Precision Mitigation
description: P2 priority. LayerCast (FP16 storage + FP32 compute) as additional precision condition on MMLU with 4 models.

results.status: planned — not started (30 GPU hours, P2)

analysis:
Lowest priority. Skip for AAAI unless reviewer explicitly asks about precision mitigation strategies. The BF16-vs-FP16 sensitivity analysis from exp-001 already shows precision is a non-issue for practical evaluation (0.0006% variance after excluding FP32).


LayerCast reduces precision×item from BF16's already-negligible 0.04% (post BF16-vs-FP16 sensitivity analysis) to ~0.02% — the improvement is unmeasurable in practice. With BF16≈FP16 (Δ=0.23pp from exp-001) and precision contributing <0.1% of variance, any mitigation strategy provides diminishing returns. The 18% inference overhead makes LayerCast cost-ineffective. Position as 1-paragraph appendix material if run; otherwise not worth the GPU hours given AAAI timeline.
